overview: The subcommittee reviewed high school homework survey results and proposed workload guidelines under behavioral health, then discussed expanding inclusive recreation and peer friendship initiatives, including the Common Ground program, under special education.

items.title: Meeting Opening and Agenda Purpose
items.summary: Chair Melanie McLaughlin opened the remote meeting and outlined the agenda covering trauma-informed practices, homework stress, and peer friendships for students with disabilities.

items.title: The NAN Project and Mental Health Awareness
items.summary: Director Stacey Schulman described Medford's partnership with The NAN Project and Eliot Community Human Services to bring young adult peer mentors into schools for suicide awareness and mental health education.

items.title: High School Homework Survey and Workload Guidelines
items.summary: Schulman and Principal Paul D'Alleva presented survey data highlighting a gap between faculty homework assignments and student-reported hours, detailing a proposal to limit homework to 30 minutes per subject across alternating subject days.

items.title: Behavioral Health Planning and Next Steps
items.summary: The subcommittee agreed to gather community input on focused mental health webinars and prepare policy recommendations for a May School Committee presentation.

items.title: Peer Friendship Initiatives and Volunteer Coordination
items.summary: McLaughlin introduced a volunteer roster and shared folder intended to support inclusive relationships, prompting discussion on Google Drive access and public records management.

items.title: Medford Recreation Adaptive Programs and Community Outreach
items.summary: Kate Quinn shared details on Medford Recreation's inclusive and adaptive offerings, and district staff and CPAC leadership agreed to coordinate on volunteer recruitment, age flexibility, and school-wide flyer distribution.

items.title: Common Ground Program Expansion
items.summary: Teachers Carla Andre and Michael Skorka reviewed the high school Common Ground model for building authentic peer friendships, with the subcommittee planning to explore budget requirements to pilot the program at lower grade levels.
